reader.requirement: At --std 85, an ALTERNATE RECORD KEY data-name-1 described in only one record description of the FD must key every record of the file by the same character positions, whichever record description (group, elementary, ODO or variable-length) a WRITE, REWRITE, READ KEY or START names, with GR3's DUPLICATES rule applied to that key.

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|CobolVersion|EditionContext|DialectBehaviors over KeyedIoEmitter.cs, FileControlKeyRules.cs, RecordLayout.cs, IndexedConnector.cs, FileRegistry.cs
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the key-window path is edition-independent; only the 2023 SUPPRESS WHEN and 2002 SOURCE phrases are refused at 85, and the 02 status on a random duplicate read is the 1985 arm of a different rule

reader.notes: The connector registers the alternate key as a byte window of the record area and every keyed verb sends the whole shared area image, so the key description's record is irrelevant to which record carries it. Out-of-line records (ODO, elementary 01) are spliced into the same area; all probes agree with the 1985 text.

refuter.evidence: Attacked what the reader's probes did not try: non-DISPLAY usages overlaying the alternate key window in another record (implicit redefinition of the FD's records in the typed-native model). Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-092/kov-003 (src/kov.cob): REC-A carries ALT-A X(4) at 5-8 and ALT-D X(2) WITH DUPLICATES at 9-10; REC-B puts PIC S9(7) PACKED-DECIMAL (length 4) at 5-8, REC-E puts PIC S9(8) BINARY (length 4) at 5-8. Printed: W1 00, W2 00, W3 IK 22 (same packed +1234567 through REC-B, no DUPLICATES), W3B 02 (packed -1234567 is a distinct key; ALT-D 'RR' a duplicate), W6 00, W7 IK 22 (same binary 1 through REC-E), W8 02; R1 00 K001 +1234567 TAIL01 (READ KEY ALT-A with the bytes saved from ALT-A after writing REC-B), R3 00 K000 +00000001 EREST001; START ALT-D = 'QQ' then N1 02 K001, N2 02 <packed prime key>, N3 00 K00Y, N4 02 K002 RR: duplicates retrieved in release order across three record descriptions, 02 while the next record has the same key, 00 at the last.
